problem: Semantic navigation lacks a language-focused evaluation: existing datasets (e.g. GOAT-Bench) have VLM-generated descriptions with many errors (67% of sampled goals) and no linguistic tags, and 2D feature maps in zero-shot methods collapse vertical context and fine-grained attributes/relations.
motivation: Natural-language goals are the most natural way to specify targets, but we cannot tell how well agents ground attributes and spatial relations. Flattening features into one 2D map merges stacked objects and drops height cues needed for spatial relations.
key_idea: Build a multi-layer (height-sliced) top-down CLIP-patch feature map queried with vanilla similarity, VLM, or a relation graph, and use a two-phase explore-and-exploit navigation, evaluated on a new manually validated, linguistically tagged multi-object language navigation benchmark.
insight: Height layering preserves fine-grained attribute and relation information: 1 layer gives SR 29.7 vs 39.5 with 3 layers, and vanilla MLFM beats 2D OneMap-v2 on all spatial relations. Structured relation-graph querying beats prompting a VLM on top-down projections, since VLMs misread them as egocentric views; the two-phase detector-then-map scheme is a large gain on its own (OneMap 15.3 to OneMap-v2 26.7 SR). Feature type and detector choice strongly affect particular attributes (texture, state).
method: Multi-layer feature map: M in R^{L x h x w x f_d}; SED CLIP patch features are back-projected with depth into a 3D point cloud and binned into L=3 height layers at 6 cm cells.

EAE-E two-phase navigation: for the first ~40% of the step budget a goal is accepted only if both the map similarity and a YOLO-World detection agree; afterwards the agent relies on the map alone. Unexplored areas use VLFM frontier exploration and an A* planner.
MLFM-vanilla querying: cosine similarity between stored features and the text query with a threshold, then take the best cell.

MLFM-VLM querying: target and reference locations are colored red/blue with the agent as a green square, per-layer tiles are sent to GPT (GPT-4 in main text, GPT-5 in appendix) to infer the relation, which is compared to the query relation via CLIP text similarity.

MLFM-RGraph querying: graph nodes are candidate object locations (with map spans and visual features) and edges carry geometric relations (above/below/near/left/right/inside) with CLIP text features; the highest target-relation-reference triplet score wins.

Dataset/task: a multi-object language navigation task with a benchmark built on HSSD, with GT attributes turned into descriptions by GPT-4, manually validated, tagged with attribute types and spatial relations from 3D boxes, three sequential goals per episode, and multiple valid targets per description.

setting.backbone: SED CLIP patch features + YOLO-World detector + A* planner (frozen, zero-shot); GPT-4/GPT-5 for the VLM variant
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + GPS/compass, language goal description
setting.action_space: low-level: move forward 25 cm, turn left/right 30°, found

numbers.backbone: SED CLIP patch + YOLO-World, 3 layers, 6 cm
numbers.extra: EAE 40%; mean of 5 runs, std ±2.5; the three-goal episode must succeed each goal within 1.5 m and 500 steps
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Performance), row 10 MLFM-RGraph; ablation tables give the same 39.5/14.9

numbers.backbone: SED CLIP patch + YOLO-World + GPT for relation reasoning

numbers.extra: language goals only; split not stated in paper (assumed val-unseen)
numbers.evidence: Table on GOAT-Bench: MLFM-RGraph 24.2 SR, 21.5 SPL vs Modular GOAT 21.5/16.2

numbers_note: Which split the new-dataset tables use is not explicitly stated (the text says test split evaluation); the GOAT-Bench split is also not stated. Tables also report per-attribute and per-relation SR, not extracted here.
results: MLFM-RGraph reaches SR 39.5 / SPL 14.9 on the new benchmark, above the best 2D map baseline OneMap-v2 (26.7/10.1) and the egocentric-image-map baseline (35.1/10.9). On GOAT-Bench language goals it gets 24.2 SR / 21.5 SPL versus Modular GOAT's 21.5 / 16.2.
limitations: The dataset lacks coreference, negation, action directives and multi-object relations; bounding-box-based relation labels and fixed proximity thresholds are approximate.
The method fails on texture and state attributes (limited by the feature extractor and detector), and RGraph confuses inside/above/on when both objects fall in the same layer.
Overall SR remains low (<40%) with high variance (±2.5); about half the failures are running out of time, and evaluation takes ~8 h on an A40.
